title: Binary search
summary: One closed interval, three outcomes: exact match, left bound, right bound—and searching on the answer.

clips.title: The search interval
clips.question: In closed-interval binary search, what do left and right mean, and when does the loop stop?

scenes.say: Binary search, question one. In a closed-interval binary search, what do left and right mean, and when does the loop stop? Pause and answer out loud.

props.question: Closed interval: what do left and right mean, and when does the loop stop?

scenes.say: Treat the search space as a closed interval: both ends are inclusive, so right starts at the last index. The loop runs while left is less than or equal to right, and stops when the interval is empty. Every update excludes mid, because mid has already been checked.

Search for nine. The interval starts as the whole array. Mid is index three, holding seven, which is too small, so left jumps to mid plus one. Now mid holds eleven, which is too big, so right drops to mid minus one. The interval is a single cell. Mid holds nine, so we return its index. Three probes instead of eight.
One more habit: compute mid as left plus half the distance to right. Adding left and right first can overflow an int on large arrays.

props.sub: Not (left + right) / 2 — the sum can overflow an int on large arrays.

clips.title: First and last occurrence
clips.question: With duplicates, how do you find the first and the last occurrence of a target?

scenes.say: Question two. With duplicates, how do you find the first and the last occurrence of a target? Pause and answer out loud.

props.question: With duplicates, how do you find the first and last occurrence?

scenes.say: The template stays the same. Only the equal branch changes. For the left bound, when mid equals the target, keep searching left with right equals mid minus one, and return left after the loop. For the right bound, search right with left equals mid plus one, and return right.

left.label: Left bound · first occurrence
left.title: Lock the left edge
left.body: Returns left (check it is in range and equal).

right.label: Right bound · last occurrence
right.title: Lock the right edge
right.body: Returns right (check it is in range and equal).

scenes.say: Find the first two in this array. Mid lands on a two, but instead of returning, right moves to mid minus one. Mid lands on the one, which is too small, so left steps forward. Mid lands on a two again, and right moves once more. Now left has crossed right, and the loop ends. Left sits on index one, the first two.

steps.note: Loop ends: left is the first 2

scenes.say: So all three searches share one skeleton. Exact match returns mid. Left bound shrinks right on a match and returns left. Right bound shrinks left on a match and returns right.

clips.title: Search on the answer
clips.question: When can you binary search something that is not a sorted array?

scenes.say: Question three. When can you binary search something that is not a sorted array? Pause and answer out loud.

props.question: When can you binary search something that is not a sorted array?

scenes.say: Whenever a yes or no check is monotonic. False, false, false, then true from some point on. Binary search finds that boundary, the first true.

props.text: F F F T T T T
props.sub: If check(x) flips from false to true exactly once, binary search finds the first true.

scenes.say: Mid is true, so the answer is here or earlier, and right moves to mid minus one. Next, mid is false, so left moves past it. False again, and left moves again. Now left has crossed right, and it rests on the first true. Return left.

steps.note: Answer is here or earlier: right = mid − 1
left rests on the first true

scenes.say: In code, the shape is familiar. Search between the lowest and highest possible answers. If mid satisfies the check, try smaller by moving right. Otherwise, try larger by moving left. When the loop ends, left is the smallest value that passes.

props.title: Binary search on the answer

highlights.note: lo / hi must cover every possible answer
Passes: the answer is mid or smaller
left is the first passing value

scenes.say: To recap. Use a closed interval and loop while left is at most right. Compute mid without overflow. The equal branch decides exact, left, or right bound. And any monotonic check can be searched the same way.

items.text: Closed interval, loop while left ≤ right.
The equal branch picks exact, left, or right bound.
Any monotonic check can be searched.
